author_or_org: Jin Jia, Zhiling Deng, Zhuangbin Chen, Yingqi Wang, Zibin Zheng

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: As LLM-based multi-agent systems are increasingly deployed for complex tasks, ensuring their reliability has become a pressing challenge.
claims.quote: As LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) are increasingly deployed for complex tasks, ensuring their reliability has become a pressing challenge.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Because MAS coordinate through unstructured natural language rather than rigid protocols, they are prone to semantic failures such as hallucinations, misinterpreted instructions, and reasoning drift that propagate silently without runtime exceptions.
claims.quote: Since MAS coordinate through unstructured natural language rather than rigid protocols, they are prone to semantic failures (e.g., hallucinations, misinterpreted instructions, and reasoning drift) that propagate silently without raising runtime exceptions.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: Prevailing evaluation approaches measure only end-to-end task success, offering limited insight into how failures arise or how effectively agents recover.
claims.quote: Prevailing evaluation approaches, which measure only end-to-end task success, offer limited insight into how these failures arise or how effectively agents recover from them.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: MAS-FIRE defines a taxonomy of 15 fault types covering intra-agent cognitive errors and inter-agent coordination failures, injected via three non-invasive mechanisms: prompt modification, response rewriting, and message routing manipulation.
claims.quote: We define a taxonomy of 15 fault types covering intra-agent cognitive errors and inter-agent coordination failures, and inject them via three non-invasive mechanisms: prompt modification, response rewriting, and message routing manipulation.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Applying MAS-FIRE to three representative MAS architectures yielded fault-tolerant behaviors organized into four tiers: mechanism, rule, prompt, and reasoning.
claims.quote: Applying MAS-FIRE to three representative MAS architectures, we uncover a rich set of fault-tolerant behaviors that we organize into four tiers: mechanism, rule, prompt, and reasoning.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: Stronger foundation models do not uniformly improve robustness.
claims.quote: Our findings reveal that stronger foundation models do not uniformly improve robustness.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: Architectural topology plays an equally decisive role, with iterative, closed-loop designs neutralizing over 40% of faults that cause catastrophic collapse in linear workflows.
claims.quote: We further show that architectural topology plays an equally decisive role, with iterative, closed-loop designs neutralizing over 40% of faults that cause catastrophic collapse in linear workflows.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: MAS-FIRE provides process-level observability and actionable guidance to systematically improve multi-agent systems.
claims.quote: MAS-FIRE provides the process-level observability and actionable guidance needed to systematically improve multi-agent systems.
